description: Tests and benchmarks Claude Code skills empirically with a fast pass/fail mode and a full baseline-comparison pipeline.

evals.name: quick-mode-setup
evals.prompt: Paths are relative to the repository root, and every file you write must use only repo-relative paths (no absolute paths, no home directories). DRY-RUN SIMULATION RULES: you cannot call AskUserQuestion and you cannot launch sub-agents. Every time the procedure would ask the operator something, write the question and the option labels into OUTDIR/transcript.md, then use the simulated operator answer given below (if none is given, choose the first option). Record in transcript.md which numbered step you are executing. Never modify any file under evals/skill-tester/fixtures or outside OUTDIR; copy what you need into OUTDIR first. OUTDIR is supplied by the dispatcher. The operator says: 'Quickly check my note-formatter skill, it lives in evals/skill-tester/fixtures/note-formatter.' Simulated operator answers: the skill is already located; testing mode is the fast pass/fail one with no baseline; two scenarios: (1) a mixed list of feature/bug/docs/refactor bullets gets grouped in the documented order, (2) a bullet without an issue number is rendered with (#none); a good response follows the skill's rules exactly; no pressure testing is wanted. Carry the work through creating the eval files only, stop before running any agent, and describe in transcript.md what the next phase would do. Work under OUTDIR/evals/note-formatter/ using the standard evals directory layout.
evals.expected_output: evals.json with the required fields and a testing_validation_coverage block (2 declared, 2 covered), one eval_metadata.json per eval with valid assertion types, workspace/iteration-1 created, and no baseline directories or benchmark.json.

uncovered: Mode selection, Full Pipeline branch: no eval runs Full Pipeline's own setup (Step 1.3 workspace creation and Phase 3 outputs); eval 3 aggregates a prebuilt workspace and eval 4 only plans dispatch paths. The Quick branch is covered by eval 1.
Trigger phrases: confirm skill activates on 'run evals on skill-X', 'benchmark this skill', 'validate skill performance', 'compare skill vs. baseline', 'test skill effectiveness'
Non-triggers: confirm skill does NOT activate on 'review my skill structure', 'create a new skill', 'fix this PR'
Smoke test: scripts/smoke_test.py passes (covered by the persisted smoke test, not by these evals)
